question: According to press reports1, the Commission is considering setting up a European intelligence service under the direct authority of its President, Ursula von der Leyen.

This structure would build on the EU Intelligence and Situation Centre (INTCEN), report to the DirectorateGeneral for International Partnerships and bypass existing services such as the European External Action Service and the Vice-President of the Commission/High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.

The plan raises many questions about its legitimacy, its legal basis, its impact on the sovereignty of the Member States and the lack of democratic consultation at this stage. In accordance with the Treaties2, intelligence and internal security are matters of national competence, and any European initiative in this area must comply strictly with the principle of subsidiarity. 1.
Can the Commission confirm the existence of this plan, which would encroach directly on the sovereign powers of the Member States in the area of intelligence?
What is the legal basis and what are the tasks and governance envisaged for this structure?
Why have Member States and the European Parliament not been formally consulted at this stage?
